readerTitle: Why Enterprise built its car rental business away from the airport
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Enterprise Rent-A-Car) + 가상 적용 (장부 대행 회사, 청소용품 유통업체)
insight: 집중 전략은 시장을 작게 고르는 것이 아니라, 넓은 경쟁자가 평균 고객에 맞추느라 잘 맞추지 못하는 고객 집단을 골라 사업 전체를 그들에게 맞추는 것이다.
misconception: 작은 시장이나 작은 회사면 그 자체로 집중 전략이다. 고객을 좁히면 성장을 포기하는 것이다.

sources.text: Porter, M. (1980). Competitive Strategy. Free Press. (focus as a generic strategy)
Enterprise Mobility, company history (founded 1957 in St. Louis by Jack Taylor; home-city replacement rentals)

factChecks.note: Enterprise 창업 연도(1957년), 창업자(Jack Taylor), 출발 도시(St. Louis), 리스 사업으로 시작했다는 점을 회사 공식 역사 자료로 다시 확인하세요.
정비·사고로 차를 맡긴 고객 대상 '대차(replacement rental)'와 보험사·정비소 관계에 집중했다는 점, 'We'll pick you up' 서비스는 널리 알려진 내용이나 시작 시점은 자료마다 다릅니다. 카드에는 시점을 적지 않았습니다.
'미국 최대 규모 렌터카 회사 중 하나'라는 표현과 2007년 Alamo·National 인수(Vanguard Car Rental)를 통한 공항 시장 확장을 게시 전 확인하세요.
동네 지점 임대료가 공항 카운터보다 낮다는 점은 일반적 논리로 제시했으며 구체적 수치는 쓰지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Why Enterprise built its car rental business away from the airport
body: For decades, the big car rental brands fought over the same place: the airport counter.
Enterprise mostly stayed out of that fight. It opened small offices in ordinary neighborhoods instead, and grew into one of the largest rental car companies in the United States.

image.label: A small neighborhood rental office next to a busy airport in the distance
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 앞쪽에 동네 골목의 작은 렌터카 사무실과 차 두 대, 뒤쪽 멀리 붐비는 공항과 줄 선 카운터. 실제 회사 로고와 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Your bookkeeping firm is losing to bigger players.
body: You run a six-person bookkeeping firm. National firms win clients with brand names. Cheap online services win on price. Your clients are a random mix: shops, builders, a few clinics, two restaurants.

options.text: Keep serving any small business, and cut prices to win more clients
options.feedback: You gain some price-sensitive clients, but you are fighting the cheapest rival on its own ground. Your costs are higher, so the margin goes first.

options.text: Serve only restaurants, and shape your process around their needs
options.feedback: You give up clients outside that group. In return you can master tips, food costs and payroll swings that general firms handle poorly.

options.text: Add more services so every client gets everything
options.feedback: More services can raise value per client. But you'd still be a general firm, just with higher costs, and a mixed client list makes it hard to get great at anything.

cards.title: A rental for people whose car is in the shop.
body: Jack Taylor started Enterprise in St. Louis in 1957. Its core customer was not the business traveler landing at an airport. It was the local driver whose own car was being repaired after a breakdown or accident.

That customer needs a car near home, often paid for by an insurer, for days or weeks. So Enterprise built neighborhood offices, worked closely with insurance adjusters and repair shops, and became known for picking customers up.

cards.title: Focus
body: **Focus** means choosing a narrow group of customers and shaping the whole business around what they need.

Inside that group, a focused business can win in one of two ways: lower cost for those customers, or something those customers value more. Enterprise did a bit of both for people renting while their car was repaired.

image.label: A wide target hit loosely versus a small target hit dead center
image.brief: 두 개의 과녁 비교 인포그래픽. 왼쪽 큰 과녁에는 화살이 흩어져 있고 "Everyone" 라벨, 오른쪽 작은 과녁에는 화살이 정중앙에 모여 있고 "One group, served fully" 라벨.

cards.title: Broad rivals are built for the average customer.
body: Airport rental companies were designed for travelers: big counters, long opening hours, one-way trips. A local customer with a car in the shop pays for much of that without needing it.

Enterprise fit its costs and service to that one job. Neighborhood offices are cheaper to run than prime airport space, and insurer relationships brought a steady flow of customers. **A broad rival over-serves some needs and under-serves others.** A focused one fixes both.
cards.softwareNote: This is why vertical software works. A booking tool built only for dental clinics can handle insurance codes and recall reminders that a general scheduling app never will.

cards.eyebrow: Small is not the same as focused
cards.title: The group has to need something different.
body: A corner shop that sells a bit of everything to everyone nearby is small, not focused. It serves the same needs as the big store, just with fewer resources.

Focus pays only when your chosen customers truly differ: in what they need, how they buy, or what it costs to serve them. If their needs match everyone else's, the big player already serves them well, and being narrow just limits you.

cards.title: Narrow ground can move under you.
list: **The group shrinks:** if the need fades, so does the business.
**A big rival moves in:** it may build a version just for your customers.
**Growth blurs the focus:** chasing new groups can bring back the average-customer problem.
cards.callout: Enterprise did later expand to airports, largely by buying other rental brands. Growing beyond a niche usually means building a separate system, not stretching the old one.

cards.title: Now it's a cleaning supplies distributor.
body: You run a regional distributor of cleaning supplies. A national distributor has a bigger catalog and lower prices on bulk orders. Which move is a real focus strategy?

options.text: Grow the catalog to match the national distributor
options.feedback: You fight on the rival's strongest ground. Its scale buys lower prices on every item you add.

options.text: Serve only medical clinics, with infection-control products, compliance paperwork and fast restocking
options.feedback: You give up general buyers. In return you meet needs the national catalog treats as an afterthought, and clinics value that more than the last few cents.
Friendly service helps, but small businesses are too varied to design around. It is narrower in name, not in what you actually do.

cards.title: Pick the customers a broad rival serves badly, then build everything for them.
body: Focus is not about being small. It works when one group's needs are different enough that a business built for everyone fits them poorly.
**Try it today:** list your three best customers. What do they need that a big competitor handles badly? Write one thing you could change to serve only them better.

image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 여러 자물쇠 중 하나에만 딱 맞게 깎인 열쇠가 꽂혀 열리는 장면. 텍스트 없음.
